newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via term system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via term system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is expected to add temporary reserves to the U.S. banking system on Thursday through a round of term system repurchase agreements, analysts said.
"We expect a term system RP...Our best guess is a four-day operation but a longer (one) is possible," said Dana Saporta, economist at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
She put the daily average add need at about $9.6 billion for the current two-week reserve maintenance period, which started on Thursday.
She added the Fed's add need is likely to grow over the next few weeks, raising the odds for a coupon pass, possibly in the middle of next week.

Marc Wanshel, economist at J.P. Morgan's Morgan Guaranty Trust Co, sees "a large ($8-$10) billion 5-day RP, which would cover the long holiday weekend and put a strong base in place for the quarter ended next Monday," he said in a statement.

The PSA The Bond Market Trade Association has recommended an early close to the U.S. Treasury market on Thursday ahead of the Good Friday holiday. Market activity is expected to come to a halt by 1400 EST/1900 GMT.
At 0930 EST/1430 GMT, federal funds were quoted at 5-5/8, above the Fed's current target rate of 5.50 percent.
